steps.body: When two groups come together, count every object in both groups to find how many there are in all.
steps.narration: When two groups come together, count every object in both groups to find how many there are in all.

widget.prompt: Fill the frame to show 3 counters, then 2 more. How many in all?

commonCounts.feedback: That fills only the first group. Two more counters still need a square each.
That fills only the second group. The first 3 counters count too.

widget.missFeedback: Fill one square at a time, counting as you go, until the frame shows the number you need.
widget.successFeedback: Five squares filled — 3 and 2 together make 5.

predict.prompt: One group has 3 blocks. Another has 2. What happens when you put them together?
predict.reveal: Putting together two groups that each have something in them always makes MORE, because the second group's objects join the first.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents koa join groups.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for koa join groups must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines koa join groups.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: Counting every object in both groups gives 5.

widget.prompt: One group has 3 blocks. Another group has 2 blocks. Put them together. How many blocks in all?

commonErrors.feedback: That counts only the first group. Putting together means counting BOTH groups.
That compares the groups instead of joining them. Count every object in both groups.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Count every object in both groups, one at a time.
